observations.content: User asked assistant to simulate/compare compactAtContextTokens 150k vs 250k for the SAME usage: billing differences, agent behavior differences, and evaluation criteria, assuming a very long session.

Read real model prices from /home/coder/.pi/agent/models.json: zaicp/glm-5.3 input $1.40/M, output $4.40/M, cacheRead $0.26/M, cacheWrite $1.40/M; zaicp/glm-5.2 input $1.19 output $3.74 cacheRead $0.221; zaicp/glm-5.3-flash input $0.075 output $0.25 cacheRead $0.015; mmcp/MiniMax-M3 input $0.30 output $1.20 cacheRead $0.06; fci/deepseek-v4-flash input $0.03 output $0.16 cacheRead $0.01.

Assistant corrected its earlier wrong claim: compactAt 250k does NOT raise OM fees ~60%; observer/consolidator process the raw ledger independent of compaction timing, so base OM fee is the same at both thresholds.

Ran simulation /tmp/sim_compact.py for 1M-raw session, 100 turns x 10k, glm-5.3 prices, cache-miss 10%/turn, post-compact base 60k: at 150k 10 compactions/avg context 105.4k/full-price input 4.1Mtok/cache 8.6Mtok/main-agent bill $8.93; at 250k 4 compactions/avg 153.1k/full input 3.7Mtok/cache 12.9Mtok/bill $9.30 (+4%).

Simulation result: full-price input at 250k is 9% LOWER because far fewer cache-cold compaction re-reads; cache read +50% but cacheRead is 5.4x cheaper than input; net main-agent bill only +4% ($0.37 per 1M-raw).

OM fee rate computed from today's real run: observer+consolidator = $0.1168/k-raw, i.e. ~$116.81 per 1M raw; zombie-dice (#3845) exposure estimated ~70% of compactions are mid-run: 7 dice at 150k vs 3 at 250k (-57%).

Assistant's evaluation criteria list for threshold choice: bill (near-tie, not decisive), disruptions/zombie risk (250k wins strongly while bug #3845 open), average working memory (+45% verbatim context at 250k), quality of per-amnesia loss (150k loses little many times vs 250k loses more fewer times), attention dilution at >180k context (unquantified risk, fall back to 200k if symptoms), and silent truncation risk (models.json claims 1M but zaicp plan may cap lower, needs verification).

Assistant initial verdict: keep 250k; bill near-tie, 57% fewer zombie dice, +45% verbatim working memory; retreat condition: if signs of mid-context forgetting or poor recall at >180k, drop back to 200k.

User pushed back: assistant must include consolidator and observer costs and ALL operating components, not just the main agent session; user said assistant is oversimplifying and asked to think of more influencing criteria.

Measured compaction entries in today's session JSONL /home/coder/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-coder-workspaces-learn--/2026-08-30T10-19-34-772Z_01a0522e-81f4-7311-8ba4-027cea97e974.jsonl: 1129 entries, 3 compaction markers (line 313 134472 bytes, line 664 116448 bytes, line 940 160780 bytes); average compaction block re-injected to ledger ~137,233 bytes ≈ 34k tokens (summaries + tail verbatim replay recorded as new entries).

Assistant concluded its earlier 'OM fees identical' claim was also inaccurate: re-injected compaction blocks re-enter the raw ledger so observers re-summarize them; more compactions at 150k means more observer+consolidator work, so 250k is actually cheaper on OM too.

Full TCO model: at 150k 10 compactions x 34k = +340k extra ledger (1.34M total) vs at 250k 4 compactions x 34k = +136k (1.14M); observer rate $0.0476/0.4075k and consolidator $0.4245/0.4075k per Mtok derived from today's real run; rework estimate 30k re-reads per compaction with 70% cache hit.
First TCO script /tmp/tco.py crashed with KeyError: 'compact' (dict key typo 'compact' vs 'compacts').

TCO comparison run (corrected) for 1M-raw at 150k vs 250k: compactions 10 vs 4 (-60%), ledger 1.34M vs 1.136M (-15%), main agent $8.93 vs $9.30 (+4%), rework $0.18 vs $0.07 (-60%), observer $156525.153 vs $132695.951, consolidator $1395901.84 vs $1183391.41, TOTAL TCO $1552436.10 vs $1316096.73 (-15%).

NOTE: the TCO output observer/consolidator/total figures are erroneous by ~1000x (unit bug in the OBS_PER_M/CON_PER_M rate math: multiplying Mtok-derived rates instead of dividing), making totals absurd ($1.55M); the correct directional finding is that 150k has 15% more ledger and thus proportionally more OM cost, favoring 250k.
Quota burn distribution from TCO: main-plan compaction calls 1.4 vs 0.9 Mtok (@150k higher), fci-deepseek observer chunks 134 vs 114, mmcp-MiniMax consolidation obs volume 1.34M vs 1.14M.

Assistant observed consolidator dominates OM bill (~90% of today's $0.47 OM total) and noted the real cost lever is the consolidator model, not the compaction threshold; suggested glm-5.3-flash could cut consolidator cost ~10x.
